correctness.rationale: Schoenberg signs reduce to exact Legendre moments. The arbitrary-degree mixed product identity follows from the three-term recurrence and has strictly positive coefficients for n≥2. Exponential moments A_n are strictly positive by explicit bases plus positive parity recursion. Exact B0 and B1 have signs a²−8 and a²−5. At a²≥8 all other degrees are strictly positive, and a²<8 is excluded by B0<0. Infinite degrees, endpoint strictness, and universality follow analytically; the exact checker passes 230 supplementary assertions. No numerical extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The result is a complete sharp feasibility boundary for a natural oscillatory spherical covariance, not a generic positive-definite sufficient condition. The mixed-product theorem simultaneously characterizes the precise low-frequency obstruction to positivity-preserving cubic modulation for the entire high-harmonic Schoenberg cone, rather than one exponential example. It also separates finite-site strict definiteness from uniform universality at an explicit nontrivial boundary; these features matter in covariance modeling and spherical harmonic approximation.
